Further analyses reveal systematic policy-specific kinematics after controlling for scene context, whereas the evaluated discrete style labels provide limited additional explanatory power. Code, checkpoints, and the metric will be released.
  </details>

- **[Japanese Handwriting Generation Based on Human Preference Feedback Using Direct Preference Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14743)**  `arXiv:2610.14743`  
  _Wakana Kuwata, Ryota Mibayashi, Masanori Tani, Hiroaki Ohshima_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  We propose a Japanese handwriting generation framework that integrates human preference feedback using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to align generative models with human cognitive and stylistic preferences. While font generation technologies leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks and diffusion models have advanced significantly, applying these approaches to handwriting generation presents unique challenges. Font generation is a deterministic process yielding consistent styles. Handwriting generation, on the other hand, is inherently non-deterministic. In handwriting, glyph shapes never match exactly even when the same writer writes the same character. We define this shape difference as handwriting variability. Although this variability is essential for conveying the natural quality of human writing, it complicates model training and substantially increases data collection costs to capture diverse distribution patterns. To address these limitations, we incorporate human perceptual feedback into the training loop of handwriting generation. While collecting extensive handwritten data is costly, evaluating pairwise preferences between two generated samples remains very easy for humans. Applying DPO, an efficient RL-free preference optimization method, to our generation model enables high-quality handwriting generation without relying on large-scale dataset collection. Experimental results across four distinct Japanese handwriting styles demonstrate that DPO-based training enhances overall structural accuracy. However, in highly complex styles with significant variability, such as brush pen writing, the model fails to capture style-specific features. These findings highlight a critical challenge in extending DPO to complex handwriting styles.
  </details>

- **[Align-VAE: Aligning Attention and Geometry in VecSet VAEs for 3D Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14734)**  `arXiv:2610.14734`  
  _Huaizhi Qu, Mingxin Yang, Xintong Han, Fangneng Zhan, Chunchao Guo_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Set-based variational autoencoders (VecSet VAEs) represent 3D shapes as compact sets of latent tokens. Although each token originates from a query at a sampled surface location, whether these latents truly align with geometry remains unclear. We investigate this alignment and identify four issues: (i) attention-sink-like tokens that attract queries from across the shape; (ii) spatially periodic repetitions in decoder attention responses; (iii) mismatched normal information in encoder and decoder query features; and (iv) missing supervision of the intrinsic relation between signed distance fields and surface normals. To address these issues, we introduce Align-VAE with four corresponding modifications: (i) a shared bank of learnable decoder tokens provides a workspace for global computation; (ii) distance-biased cross-attention guides retrieval toward nearby predicted spatial anchors; (iii) normal-free encoder queries align the two stages' access to normal information while retaining normals in the encoder keys and values; and (iv) a screened Poisson-inspired regularizer supervises surface values and normal-direction derivatives. These changes align latent retrieval and field prediction with geometry without enlarging the per-shape code. On the ABO dataset, Align-VAE reduces Chamfer distance by 26.6% compared to the standard VecSet VAE.
  </details>

- **[LightVAE: Towards Compact and Efficient Video Autoencoders](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14726)**  `arXiv:2610.14726`  
  _Shiqiao Gu, Yang Yong, Fengjun Zhong, Ruihao Gong, Chengtao Lv, Xiangyu Fan, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Latent diffusion models enable high-quality video generation, but video VAE encoding and decoding remain computationally expensive. Existing methods use stage-specific lightweight operators, yet either constrain spatial and temporal computation jointly or remove temporal computation altogether, without distinguishing their compression sensitivities in pretrained Conv3D. To address these limitations, we present LightVAE, a compression framework that exploits redundancy in temporal modeling and network depth. LightVAE exactly reparameterizes eligible causal Conv3D layers into an aggregate spatial response and a difference-driven temporal correction. Based on their distinct compression sensitivities, temporal low-rank compression (TLR) keeps the aggregate spatial kernel dense and applies layer-specific low-rank approximation only to the temporal correction. An algebraically equivalent folded implementation converts the arithmetic savings into practical acceleration. LightVAE further uses width-preserving block pruning to reduce depth and probe-guided feature alignment, guided by feedback from a frozen teacher suffix, to recover quality after compression. The framework also extends to video encoders. Across three video VAE backbones and two GPU platforms, LightVAE consistently accelerates decoding. For the Wan VAE family, it achieves up to $2.24\times$ and $1.11\times$ the decoding throughput of state-of-the-art efficient VAE decoders on NVIDIA H100 and RTX~5090, respectively, with higher DAVIS PSNR and lower LPIPS. On MiniMax-H3, it achieves up to $2.97\times$ the original decoding throughput while retaining 99.51\% of the original model's overall VBench-2.0 score. Our code is available atthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[PixARG: Pixel-Asynchronous Retrieval-Augmented Diffusion for Fast and Realistic Image Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14713)**  `arXiv:2610.14713`  
  _Zewei Xin, Qinya Li, Chaoyue Niu, Fan Wu_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  While diffusion models achieve impressive image generation capabilities, they suffer from high computational costs, implausible artifacts, and limited adaptability to dynamic or private data due to static, centralized training. To address these, we propose PixARG, a novel retrieval-augmented generative framework that integrates dynamic real-world image retrieval into the diffusion pipeline to simultaneously enhance efficiency and visual realism. Specifically, PixARG constructs a pixel-level affinity map between the user's text prompt and the retrieved image to guide a heterogeneous noise initialization. By modulating noise intensity across spatial regions, this mechanism preserves semantically relevant structural priors while perturbing less relevant areas, thereby significantly accelerating convergence. To accommodate this spatially non-uniform noise and ensure synchronized generation, we introduce a pixel-wise asynchronous denoising scheduler and a spatiotemporal denoiser conditioned on the affinity map. Furthermore, we derive an affinity-adaptive training objective that elegantly balances deterministic restoration with stochastic regeneration across pixels. Experiments on LAION and COYO datasets across offline, online, and user-specific settings show PixARG enhances realism and semantic alignment while drastically reducing diffusion steps.
  </details>

- **[PURE: Refining Feed-forward 3D Reconstruction with Unlabeled Post-training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14698)**  `arXiv:2610.14698`  
  _Yaolong Zhu, Peng Li, Jiahao Lu, Chengfeng Zhao, Mengfei Li, Chao Wang, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models have achieved remarkable progress through large-scale training and strong learned priors. However, they remain fragile when applied to dynamic in-the-wild videos, where non-rigid motion, occlusions, and illumination changes are prevalent. A key limitation lies in their reliance on expensive depth and camera pose annotations, which hinders scaling to diverse real-world dynamic data and restricts generalization. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{PURE}, an unlabeled post-training refinement framework that improves depth and camera estimation without requiring ground-truth supervision. Instead of relying on annotations, PURE elegantly distills robust structural knowledge from state-of-the-art 2D priors into 4D feed-forward architectures. PURE leverages relative depth constraints, affine-invariant geometry distillation, and pose refinement based on feature correspondences to stabilize geometric predictions under challenging dynamic conditions. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world dynamic benchmarks demonstrate that PURE delivers consistent improvements across multiple state-of-the-art architectures. Furthermore, our data-efficient paradigm effectively mitigates domain shifts, successfully unlocking the architectural limits of these base models in challenging, in-the-wild dynamic scenes.
  </details>

- **[Demiurge: Forging Navigable 4D Worlds via Autoregressive Video Rerendering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14685)**  `arXiv:2610.14685`  
  _Hanxin Zhu, Jianqi Ma, Cong Wang, Zhihao Hu, Junyao Gao, Tianyu He, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Recent advances in video diffusion enable novel-view video synthesis from a single input video, supporting world modeling, embodied intelligence, and robotic simulation. However, existing methods process camera trajectories independently, lacking the cross-trajectory consistency needed for coherent, navigable 4D worlds. We introduce Demiurge, an autoregressive video rerendering pipeline built on a dynamic 4D point-cloud memory cache. It promotes cross-trajectory consistency through four components: (1) an appearance video diffusion model that synthesizes photorealistic novel-view videos conditioned on the 4D memory; (2) a memory-consistent video depth completion model that aligns known-region depths with cached geometry and completes missing regions, mitigating scale ambiguity and discontinuities during memory updates; (3) memory-aware dual-stream warping that provides high-fidelity visual guidance and occlusion cues for novel-view synthesis; and (4) geometry-aware video refinement that enhances perceptual quality. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and three key capabilities: coherent spatiotemporal lattice construction over dense multi-view trajectories; large-parallax video rerendering under challenging camera motions, including 180-degree rotations with no input-view overlap; and geometry-faithful outputs that can be directly optimized into high-quality 3D Gaussian Splatting representations with minimal artifacts. Project page:this https URL.
  </details>

- **[HumanPhys: A Human-Centric Physical-World Perception Benchmark for Real-World Visual Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14679)**  `arXiv:2610.14679`  
  _Yiming Zhang, Enzhi Zhou, Junan Lin, Dulan Zhou, Weiqiang Wang, Yuge Huang, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  We introduce HumanPhys, a human-centric benchmark for real-world physical perception, and a training corpus emitted by the same pipeline. Each question targets a physically grounded quantity related to people, including depth, inter-person distance, gaze angle, displacement, velocity, heading-step trajectory, blink count, and contact-deformation strength. The rendered probes additionally test illumination inference from body and face cues and camera ego-motion, both with and without a person in the frame. All labels are derived programmatically from sensor calibration, source metadata, or renderer state, rather than written by annotators or produced by estimators on the benchmark frames. HumanPhys systematically probes six dimensions of human-centric physical perception: spatial state, kinematics, blink events, deformation, illumination, and camera pose. To the best of our knowledge, no existing MLLM benchmark-and-training corpus jointly supervises this set of human-centered physical quantities under direct metadata- or renderer-derived labels. The six dimensions appear only partially dissociable across the tested MLLMs. We benchmark a range of open- and closed-source MLLMs on HumanPhys and find that all six capability dimensions remain challenging for current models. We hope HumanPhys will support future research on multimodal systems that perceive and reason about people in the physical world.
  </details>

- **[Competition Domains Matter: Selective Head Globalization for Training-Free Sparse Attention in Video Diffusion Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14672)**  `arXiv:2610.14672`  
  _Tiantian Liu, Meng Wan, Zhiqiang Liang, Jue Wang, Ningming Nie, Yangang Wang_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Training-free sparse attention is a practical route to efficient video diffusion transformer inference, yet existing methods typically fix the competition domain at each query row for every attention head. Prior work primarily addresses how to estimate token-level importance within this fixed domain; whether the domain itself should adapt to head heterogeneity remains under-specified. We introduce EG-Sparse, a training-free framework that routes low-entropy heads to a grouped cross-head pool while retaining per-row local selection for high-entropy heads, using only scores already materialized by the sparse pipeline. A controlled diagnostic fixes the ranking score and varies only the competition rule: grouped cross-head selection reduces low-entropy-head reconstruction error by 9.8%, whereas forcing high-entropy heads into an all-head global pool increases it by 7.9%. Across four configurations, EG-Sparse achieves higher video quality while reducing attention density and GPU denoising latency compared with strong training-free sparse-attention baselines. Mechanism ablations further show that selective domain adaptation outperforms uniform, random, and fixed domain-assignment policies. These results support competition-domain adaptation as a distinct design axis within centroid-guided training-free sparse attention.
  </details>

- **[SPARE: Shared Perception and Adaptive Retrieval of Evidence for Streaming Video Understanding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14671)**  `arXiv:2610.14671`  
  _Senbin Xu, Zijun Zhang, Xinhua Wu, Li He, Jubo Feng, Li Qiao, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Streaming video understanding requires answering questions from the observed video, with evidence drawn from recent observations or earlier events. Historical context can improve recall but may interfere with judgments based on recent frames. Its usefulness depends on both when it is introduced and which clips are selected, while relevance alone does not guarantee sufficient evidence for an answer. We propose SPARE, a framework that combines adaptive historical retrieval with visual encoder sharing. A lightweight gate predicts whether recent observations provide sufficient evidence to answer the question. When additional evidence is predicted to be necessary, a multimodal embedding model retrieves relevant historical clips to supplement the current context. LoRA instruction tuning trains the understanding model to use recent observations and retrieved history jointly and abstain when the evidence remains insufficient. To reduce redundant visual parameters, the understanding and retrieval branches share a visual encoder while retaining separate language backbones. Four linear adapters align the shared features with the retrieval model through distillation at the visual token and final retrieval embedding levels. With visual-only inputs, SPARE achieves 77.78% on the evaluated Real-time and Backward task groups of OVO-Bench and 73.31% on StreamingBench. Compared with Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct evaluated at 2 fps, SPARE improves accuracy by 20.68 percentage points on OVO-Bench and 14.15 percentage points on StreamingBench.
  </details>

- **[TETRIS-4DGS: Efficient Post-Training Compression of 4D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14663)**  `arXiv:2610.14663`  
  _Chengzhen Wu, Kelei Liu, Sicheng Li, Lu Yu, Yiyi Liao_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) has emerged as a powerful dynamic scene representation, supporting real-time high quality rendering but suffers from prohibitive storage overhead. Existing methods typically attempt to solve this by treating compression as a per-scene optimization problem, limiting generalizability and applicability where low-latency compression is required. In this work, we leverage existing image and video codecs and propose a generalized post-training compression framework for 4DGS to address these issues. Specifically, we apply importance-based adaptive quantization to Gaussians according to their importance levels, effectively refining bitrate allocation while remaining fully compatible with existing codecs. To further improve compression efficiency, we utilize the statistical properties of 4DGS and propose motion- and importance-aware packing to reorganize attributes into codec-friendly 2D maps. Our approach can achieve over 40x compression rate in seconds while maintaining high quality, facilitating the practical deployment of 4DGS.
  </details>

- **[TGuide: Faster Autoregressive Video Diffusion via Historical Trajectory Guidance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14657)**  `arXiv:2610.14657`  
  _Zhuo Chen, Bin Zou, Fanyue Wei, Lixin Duan, Angela Yao, Wen Li_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Can autoregressive video diffusion be accelerated further when only four denoising steps remain? Existing feature caching approaches struggle in this regime, as large feature changes between denoising timesteps undermine both direct reuse and lightweight predictors. We observe that features across video chunks remain strongly correlated at matching denoising timesteps, offering a complementary source of guidance. Building on this insight, we introduce TGuide, a framework that accelerates autoregressive video diffusion through a lightweight Anchor-Transport-Correct (ATC) predictor guided by historical sampling trajectories. Our ATC combines two complementary references: the current chunk's preceding-step features preserve its spatial structure, while the previous chunk's same-timestep features provide information at the target denoising stage. By integrating these references through spatial retrieval and adaptive correction, ATC improves velocity prediction accuracy despite the large gaps between denoising steps. To mitigate error accumulation across both denoising steps and video chunks, we train the predictor on its own autoregressive rollouts, allowing it to adapt to states shaped by its own earlier predictions. An optional confidence-aware scheduler further adjusts the quality-efficiency trade-off. Experiments on Self Forcing, Causal Forcing, and HY-WorldPlay show that TGuide preserves generation quality while achieving denoising speedups of up to $1.89\times$ over the original 4-step generators. On Self Forcing, TGuide generalizes from 81-frame training videos to 333-frame generation, approximately four times the training length, while exceeding the original model's VBench score.
  </details>

- **[Prospective Forcing: Learning to Look Ahead for Autoregressive Long Video Diffusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14654)**  `arXiv:2610.14654`  
  _Yifan Shen, Yewei Xia, Gongxu Luo, Peiyuan Zhu, Boyang Sun, Zhenhao Chen, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Autoregressive video generators synthesize long videos through chunk-wise rollouts, yet they are typically trained to predict only the immediate future. This limited prediction horizon makes it challenging to maintain video quality over extended rollouts. To address this problem, we introduce Prospective Forcing, a multi-head prediction framework that injects long-range predictive signals into autoregressive video representations. Built on a rolling-window generator, Prospective Forcing attaches lightweight, offset-specific heads that share the same conditioning information and independently predict chunks at different future temporal offsets. By extending supervision beyond the next chunk, these heads encourage the shared history representation to retain information useful for longer-horizon prediction, supporting temporally consistent generation. At inference time, we accelerate sampling by using accepted future-chunk predictions to skip full-window backbone executions. We equip the head with learnable embeddings to generate multiple candidates for the next chunk, and a learned verifier either selects a candidate or rejects all and falls back to standard autoregressive generation.
  </details>

- **[TAG: Calibrating SAM3 for Universal Image Segmentation without Dense Supervision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14651)**  `arXiv:2610.14651`  
  _Hao Zhu, Heyu Sun, Shuo Jin, Jiayu Xiao, Feng Dai_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  The recent Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3) extends powerful promptable segmentation from spatial cues to concepts, raising the prospect of a single foundation model for universal image segmentation. However, this promise often fails to translate into reliable performance on downstream segmentation tasks. In this work, we empirically identify concept recognition, rather than mask quality, as the primary bottleneck: SAM3 accurately delineates the objects it recognizes yet struggles to robustly determine which concepts are present. Driven by this, we present \textit{\underline{T}ext \underline{A}nchor re-\underline{G}rounding (\TAG{})}, a simple yet effective framework that rectifies the concept recognition of SAM3 on the target domain without dense annotations. Specifically, \TAG{} introduces an \textit{Anchor Residual Pathway} comprising image-conditioned, low-rank adapters to re-ground text anchors in the target distribution and modulate subsequent text-conditioned interactions. Guided solely by image-level category labels, \TAG{} jointly optimizes binary cross-entropy with \textit{Soft Boundary Ranking} objectives to calibrate presence confidence and distinguish present concepts from confusable negatives. Building upon this, we devise \textit{Confidence-Weighted Distillation} to couple rich semantic context of a multimodal large language model with fine-grained spatial priors of SAM3, thereby achieving effective calibration in the absence of manual annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that \TAG{} unlocks SAM3's segmentation potential with only 3.1M trainable parameters, achieving impressive performance across diverse scenarios, and notably, even surpassing leading mask-supervised methods on several metrics. \href{this https URL}{Our code will be publicly available at GitHub \faGithub}.
  </details>

- **[Can Synthetic UAV Benchmarks Be Trusted? Real-Synthetic Validation for UAV Model Selection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14647)**  `arXiv:2610.14647`  
  _Yuyi Zhi, Min Du, Bill Shi, Guodong Yuan, Junheng Liang, Peifan Liao, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Synthetic UAV imagery can expand pre-deployment test evidence when task-specific Real data are scarce, but visual plausibility or semantic label alignment alone does not establish validity for model selection. We study when Synthetic evaluation preserves the model-selection conclusions obtained from Real UAV data through two complementary cases under fixed evaluation protocols. In a requirement-specific road-debris benchmark, four language-conditioned perception systems obtain lower absolute F1 on Synthetic data, yet the point-estimate ordering and top-ranked model are preserved; bootstrap analysis yields no supported pairwise reversal, and size-matched resampling preserves the top-model decision. In contrast, a closed-set stress test on a separately materialized business corpus, using four VisDrone-compatible detectors over eight empirically supported classes, changes the point-estimate top-ranked detector and reverses three of six pairwise point-estimate preference directions. A complementary audit of five UAV business scenarios further reveals substantial Real-Synthetic mismatch in class composition, object density, and target scale, including systematic under-representation of small targets. These results show that Synthetic UAV benchmark trust is conditional: semantic coverage is insufficient, and validity must be established empirically for the task, operating regime, and model panel of interest.
  </details>

- **[DuSRFlow: Dual-Lens Super-Resolution via Parallax-Aware Flow Estimation and Complementary Reference Warping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14630)**  `arXiv:2610.14630`  
  _Fangpu Zhang, Huanjing Yue, Zifan Cui, Shaoxiong Tu, Qirui Yang, Jingyu Yang_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Dual-lens super-resolution (DuSR) aims to enhance a wide-angle low-resolution (LR) image by exploiting a telephoto reference (Ref) image. A central challenge in DuSR is reliable reference utilization under large parallax, occlusion, and cross-camera imaging discrepancies. Existing methods often employ off-the-shelf monocular optical flow models to provide geometric priors. However, their assumptions of photometric consistency and smooth motion are violated in dual-lens scenarios, leading to unreliable alignment and degraded reference-based reconstruction. To address these issues, we propose DuSRFlow, a dual-lens super-resolution framework that improves reference utilization from both correspondence learning and reference aggregation. First, we introduce DuFlowNet, a dedicated dual-lens flow estimator for robust cross-view alignment. To train DuFlowNet without ground-truth flow annotations, we develop a real--synthetic data fusion strategy that composites synthetic foreground objects onto real dual-lens image pairs, generating controllable large-parallax samples while preserving realistic cross-camera imaging characteristics. Second, we observe that reference reliability is highly spatially uneven in DuSR, where unreliable local reference responses may suppress the utilization of reliable cues. We therefore propose a Complementary Reference Warping strategy that coordinates patch-based warping and kernel-free-guided deformable warping according to local reference reliability, producing a more reliable reference representation before LR--Ref fusion. In addition, we construct DuSR-RealV2, a challenging real-world benchmark with complex depth variations, large parallax, and occlusion. Extensive experiments on multiple DuSR benchmarks demonstrate that DuSRFlow achieves state-of-the-art performance in reconstruction quality, perceptual quality, and cross-dataset generalization.
  </details>

- **[EarthAlign: Learning Language-Aligned Representations of Earth System Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14624)**  `arXiv:2610.14624`  
  _Fadillah Adamsyah Maani, Numan Saeed, Jiaqi Ma, Dat Tien Nguyen, Youssef Wehbe, Duncan Watson-Parris, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Interpreting Earth system conditions is central to understanding environmental risks and informing decisions across weather- and climate-sensitive sectors. Existing multimodal weather systems primarily target task-specific prediction, generation, or question answering, while general-purpose alignment between Earth system data and language remains underexplored due to the limited availability of diverse language supervision grounded in meteorological conditions. To fill this gap, we introduce EarthAlign, a large-scale dataset with broad geographic coverage spanning 2000-2024 that combines 10 expert-curated natural event and disaster data sources with climatology-derived normal-weather samples. Each sample includes temporal and geospatial information and four grounded caption styles aligned with 63-variable ERA5 meteorological data. Building on EarthAlign, we introduce MeteoLIP, a dual-encoder framework for learning aligned meteorology-language representations. MeteoLIP incorporates MetTok, which uses a geolocation- and time-conditioned query to aggregate variable-specific patch embeddings into a compact sequence of meteorology tokens. To comprehensively assess Earth system multimodal representations, we introduce three downstream tasks: cross-modal retrieval, weather-condition classification, and physical variable estimation. Our experiments show that MeteoLIP improves upon the corresponding CLIP and SigLIP baselines across these tasks. Further analyses highlight the importance of meteorological input, temporal and geospatial conditioning, and multi-style supervision for meteorology-language alignment. Thus, EarthAlign and MeteoLIP provide a foundation for learning and evaluating language-aligned representations of Earth system data. Our code, dataset, and weights are publicly available atthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[EviScene: Beyond "Is It AI?" for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14609)**  `arXiv:2610.14609`  
  _ZiAn Wang, Ruiqi Liu, Zhengbo Zhang, Yi Han, Jialiang Shen, Ruoxin Chen, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Determining whether an image is AI-generated does not establish whether the situation it depicts is factually supported. We formulate Image Factuality Assessment: given an image and a generic verification instruction, a system returns a supported or refuted verdict with an evidence-grounded explanation. Without a supplied textual claim, the system must progressively refine factual questions during investigation and align external evidence with the specific situation depicted. We introduce EviLens, an expert-reviewed benchmark of 10,174 supported and refuted images from controlled construction and web collection, covering twelve factual error types and evaluating both verdict accuracy and evidence sufficiency. We develop EviScene, a multimodal ReAct agent that interleaves visual inspection, external retrieval, and evidence analysis, using new findings to refine its questions and revisit relevant image details. We train a compact policy with supervised fine-tuning on reviewed teacher trajectories, followed by privileged on-policy self-distillation applied to verified decisions from the policy's own investigations. On the 1,527-image test set, the trained Qwen3.5-9B agent achieves 79.05% balanced accuracy and a Strict Evidence Sufficiency Rate (SESR) of 52.26%, improving over the same-backbone base agent by 6.71 and 9.37 percentage points, respectively. Its SESR is the highest among the evaluatedthis http URL, models, and data will be released atthis https URLandthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[Bidirectional Adaptive Transformers for Multimodal Anomaly Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14598)**  `arXiv:2610.14598`  
  _Yuxin Jiang, Yunkang Cao, Weiming Shen_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  The effective integration of features derived from RGB images and 3D point clouds presents a substantial challenge in the field of multimodal anomaly detection (MAD). Existing MAD methods typically rely on static fusion paradigms built upon frozen pre-trained encoders. While these frameworks facilitate spatial alignment, they lack the mechanism to establish latent semantic correspondence, thereby inducing cross-modal interference that degrades anomaly discriminability.To mitigate these limitations, this study proposes a Bidirectional Adaptive Transformers (BAT) framework, which constructs comprehensive and semantically aligned multimodal representations by leveraging complementary attributes across modalities.The BAT framework introduces a Bidirectional Feature Alignment (BFA) module, which employs a mutual predictive mechanism to bridge the gap between 2D textural patterns and 3D geometric structures. This bidirectional interaction explicitly enhances the textural granularity of point cloud descriptors while augmenting the spatial contextual awareness of RGB features.To ensure that the latent representations possess sufficient informational density for alignment, BAT incorporates a parameter-efficient adaptation architecture. By utilizing lightweight image and point cloud adapters, the framework facilitates specialized fine-tuning of pre-trained models, mitigating the information loss inherent in frozen encoders.Extensive experiments conducted on MVTec 3D-AD and Eyecandies confirm that BAT achieves state-of-the-art anomaly detection performance, significantly outperforming existing MAD methods.
  </details>

- **[Attribute-Centric Vision-Language Alignment for Fine-Grained Gait Understanding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14589)**  `arXiv:2610.14589`  
  _Saihui Hou, Chenye Wang, Wenpeng Lang, Qiannan Guo, Zhengxiang Lan, Chao Fan, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Walking sequences reveal human-interpretable attributes related to body structure, posture, and motion. Gait attribute recognition provides a concrete route to fine-grained gait understanding by predicting these attributes. However, existing benchmarks provide limited fine-grained annotations, while classifier-based gait attribute recognition methods typically represent candidate classes through learned output weights rather than directly matching visual evidence with textual class representations. To address the annotation gap, we present RA-GAR, a large-scale, richly annotated multimodal benchmark for gait attribute recognition, containing 1,001 subjects, 242,729 walking sequences, and annotations for 15 static and motion gait attributes. We further propose Gait-VL, an attribute-centric vision-language alignment framework that recognizes gait attributes by matching attribute-specific multi-frame visual evidence with textual class prototypes. On the visual side, attribute-specific learnable queries aggregate RGB features across spatial locations and frames into per-attribute visual embeddings. On the language side, diverse descriptions expanded by a large language model are combined with context about relevant body regions to construct textual class prototypes. Beyond attribute recognition, we evaluate the transferability of the attribute-pretrained visual encoder by using it to replace generic upstream large vision models in identityoriented gait recognition pipelines; attribute pre-training uses no identity classification or metric-learning objectives.   </details>

- **[FrameFold: Response-Guided KV Cache Consolidation for Autoregressive Long Video Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14568)**  `arXiv:2610.14568`  
  _Muyu Liu, Mingming Liu, Hong Gu, Yuyao Zhang, Qin Lu_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  In autoregressive video generation, retaining all historical key-value (KV) states increases memory usage and per-step attention costs as videos grow longer. A fixed cache budget bounds these costs but raises the challenge of preserving historical content that supports consistent, high-quality generation. Existing methods control cache size through history selection or consolidation, yet deciding what to retain and how to limit the loss of useful content remains a shared challenge. Our analysis shows that spatial queries depend on different historical content and that higher current attention coverage does not necessarily yield better long-video quality. We introduce FrameFold, a training-free KV cache consolidation method that compares the content retrieved by the same recent historical queries before and after merging to guide both representative construction and merge selection. Exploiting temporal redundancy between adjacent historical entries, FrameFold merges their KV states into shared representatives while retaining complete spatial grids. It fits value-merging coefficients in closed form by matching conditional attention responses, then selects the merge with the lowest remaining response distortion. Under matched KV cache budgets, experiments on Self Forcing and Causal Forcing at 30 and 60 seconds and on LongLive at 120 seconds demonstrate improved consistency and visual quality. Continuous eight-minute Self Forcing rollouts further show less quality degradation than the baselines.
  </details>

- **[Adversarial Gradient Forcing for Robust Few-Step Autoregressive Video Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14553)**  `arXiv:2610.14553`  
  _Chenxi Xia, Yixuan Xu, Shan Liu, Jiapeng Wang, Maohua Li, Hanlin Tang, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Autoregressive video generation models generate videos sequentially, with each new block conditioned on previously generated blocks. By training on the model's own rollouts, Self Forcing and its follow-up methods substantially mitigate exposure bias caused by the mismatch between training- and inference-time history distributions. However, these models still suffer from error accumulation during long-horizon generation. We identify a key underlying limitation: the model remains highly sensitive to errors in its generated history, allowing small deviations to be amplified through subsequent generations. We refer to this underexplored problem as the local history robustness gap. To address this gap, we introduce Adversarial Gradient Forcing (AGF), a framework designed to improve the robustness of few-step autoregressive video models to perturbations and accumulated errors in their own generated histories. AGF uses distribution matching gradients from future block predictions to select adversarial perturbations of self-generated histories. It then jointly trains the generator on the original and perturbed histories to improve the robustness of future generation. Extensive experiments show that AGF achieves the highest VBench Total score on 60-second video generation and the best visual quality on four-minute video generation. Notably, AGF achieves such long-horizon robustness while requiring only 5-second rollouts for training.
  </details>

- **[InfraWorld: Motion-Aware World Modeling for Roadside 4D Occupancy Forecasting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14544)**  `arXiv:2610.14544`  
  _Songkai Wang, Xiaokai Bai, Lei Yang, Hui-liang Shen_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Roadside 4D occupancy forecasting predicts future semantic occupancy in a fixed infrastructure coordinate system. Roadside scenes are globally structured yet locally evolving, requiring comprehensive scene-level context while precisely modeling sparse localized motion. However, existing forecasting paradigms struggle to tackle both requirements. To address this limitation, we propose InfraWorld, a world model formulating roadside occupancy forecasting as selective state evolution. InfraWorld maintains a dense BEV state for the complete scene and persistent motion queries for moving regions, assigning complementary states to global context and local dynamics. Specifically, we propose Dynamic Query Initiation (DQI) to initialize queries in regions supported by motion in the observed history. During rollout, the dense state is updated through Long--Short Temporal Fusion (LST), which combines short-term adjacent-frame continuity with long-term motion trends to preserve stable context while capturing scene evolution. Motion-Aware Query Injection (MAQI) then refines the queries and injects confidence-weighted query information into corresponding BEV tokens, enabling targeted dynamic updates without perturbing global context. Together, InfraWorld concentrates predictive capacity on evolving traffic regions. Extensive experiments on the InfraOcc and Occ3D--nus datasets demonstrate that InfraWorld achieves state-of-the-art performance for roadside 4D occupancy forecasting while retaining its effectiveness under ego-centric settings. Code will be released.
  </details>

- **[We Have Been Interpreting Diffusion Transformer Backbone Behaviors Wrong](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14517)**  `arXiv:2610.14517`  
  _Benyuan Meng, Longtao Huang, Yang Liu, Liang Lin_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  During a network forward call, diffusion backbones naturally produce many intermediate activations. If we evaluate each activation against an identical downstream benchmarking protocol, we can plot an inverted-U-shaped curve as the depth profile: the activation's performance goes up first and then down as we go into deeper layers. This is common knowledge in the diffusion model community, which inspires many applications including the widely-adopted REPA. However, the common interpretation of this depth profile may be inaccurate and incomplete: (i) The cause of this curve has long been treated as signal granularity changing from coarse to fine, but there has been little evidence in DiT backbones. (ii) The community has been mainly studying this phenomenon in a static way, without investigating how it changes across different training setups. In this work, we show a different mechanism picture for the profile, where the prediction target (e.g., $\epsilon$, $u$, $x_0$) sits at the center. The semantically meaningful signal is only an intermediate by-product for predicting the target, while the prediction target is the real goal for the backbone. Furthermore, the choice of prediction targets as part of the training setup can predictably affect the curve's shape. With this updated interpretation, many applications of this depth profile can be better grounded and predicted. As an example, we show how to predict the near-optimal placement of REPA based on the prediction target of the training setup. The code is atthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[Compositional Concepts Erasing: Disentangling Object-Style via Domain Manifold Unlearning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14514)**  `arXiv:2610.14514`  
  _Yang Xiao, Kaiyuan Deng, Gen Li, Zinan Ling, Zhiwen Fan, Xiaolong Ma, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Diffusion models pose significant risks regarding the generation of illicit content and copyright violations. This has catalyzed the development of machine unlearning to erase harmful concepts or copyrighted styles from a model's generative repertoire without compromising its general performance. However, previous unlearning approaches on diffusion models have largely focused on either object-level or style-level removal and failed to address the challenge of object-style combination unlearning. At the same time, multiple unlearning requests often lead to catastrophic forgetting. To address these challenges, we propose Domain Manifold Unlearning (DMU), which uses an EMA-updated feature proxy extracted from intermediate diffusion features to represent the retained target-object direction. As a lightweight estimating representation of an object, DMU enables selective unlearning of domain-specific components in a specific object while preserving other semantic representations, thereby significantly enhancing robustness in multiple combination unlearning scenarios. Extensive experiments show that DMU significantly mitigates catastrophic forgetting, outperforming state-of-the-art methods of batch unlearning and sequential unlearning.
  </details>

- **[TartanMatch: Towards Universal Dense Correspondence Across Modalities](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14513)**  `arXiv:2610.14513`  
  _Hyeokjoon Kwon, Jiting Cai, Ruogu Li, Kritan Bhandari, Geethika Hemkumar, Parv Maheshwari, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Robotic platforms combine multi-modal sensors to operate across diverse conditions, but most dense correspondence methods are limited to RGB-RGB or a small set of modality pairs. Training a model for each modality pair scales poorly with the number of sensors and forgoes potential positive transfer across modality pairs. We introduce TartanMatch, a unified model for dense correspondence across all 25 ordered pairs among RGB, event, thermal, depth, and projected LiDAR. TartanMatch adapts an RGB-pretrained correspondence model to all modality pairs within one shared network using lightweight modality adaptation and a mixture of real and synthetic data. On zero-shot real-world benchmarks, TartanMatch reduces Endpoint Error (EPE) over the strongest baselines by 61.9% for cross-modal matching and 49.6% for same-modal matching. We further show that joint training across all modality pairs improves average matching accuracy over pair-specific training, especially on challenging cross-modal pairs. These results demonstrate that a single model achieves broad multi-modal coverage and state-of-the-art matching accuracy.
  </details>

- **[Spatiotemporal Recognition of Abdominal Wall Layers During Optical Trocar Entry](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14512)**  `arXiv:2610.14512`  
  _Shreeram Athreya, Andrew Melehy, Carter Prentice, Michael Robinson, Corey Arnold, James Wu, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Objective. To evaluate whether spatial context and temporal modeling improve tissue recognition during optical trocar entry, where multiple abdominal-wall tissues may be visible simultaneously. Methods. We retrospectively analyzed 71 recordings with 1,516 annotated keyframes and 29,151 clinician-annotated sectors. Each frame was divided into 28 polar-grid sectors assigned to nine tissue classes. Color, neighboring-sector, and positional features were used by a gradient-boosted emission classifier. The full pipeline added learned temporal smoothing, spatial regularization, an anatomically ordered hidden Markov model, and posterior blending. Five-fold cross-validation was grouped by recording, with cross-fitting to prevent within-recording leakage. Primary evaluation used clinician-derived targets; ablations assessed classification, probability quality, spatial consistency, and peritoneum-or-deeper onset timing. Results. The complete pipeline achieved accuracy 0.646, macro-F1 0.507, and macro-AUROC 0.882, versus 0.600, 0.440, and 0.861 for emissions alone. Macro-F1 improved by 0.066 across all five folds. Label changes decreased from 66.2 to 19.5 per sector-minute, and median onset error decreased from 15.58 to 2.45 seconds. Frames with a tissue-depth-code span of at least three decreased from 53% to 26%, versus 22% for clinician annotations. Performance remained limited for preperitoneal fat and bowel, and the full model retained a 44% premature-onset proportion. Conclusions. Combining appearance, spatial context, and temporal constraints improved retrospective tissue recognition and onset localization. Tissue-specific limitations, residual timing errors, and reliance on future observations warrant external validation and prospective evaluation of causal models before clinical use.
  </details>

- **[DSR-Net: Learning Dynamic Skeletal Relations for 3D Human Pose Estimation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14499)**  `arXiv:2610.14499`  
  _Fan Li, Jian Xiang, LinLin Xue, Yuwei Gao_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>

Existing methods typically rely on fixed skeletal topologies in Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) or implicitly capture joint relations through attention mechanisms, limiting their adaptability to diverse motion patterns. To address this issue,we proposeDSR-Net, a dynamic structural representation learning framework for 3D human pose estimation. Specifically, a Dynamic Skeletal Relation (DSR) module is introduced to learn adaptive inter-joint dependencies beyond predefined skeletal connections. Based on the learned relations, a hierarchical relation-aware fusion strategy is developed to facilitate effective interaction between structural and temporal representations. In addition, a lightweight Residual Skeletal Recalibration Module (RSRM) is designed to enhance the stability of structure-aware features with minimal computational overhead. Extensive experiments on Human3.6M and MPI-INF-3DHP demonstrate that DSR-Net achieves MPJPEs of 37.9 mm and 14.9 mm, respectively, consistently improving over strong baselines. - **[FreeCHROMA: Generative Chroma Keying from Unaligned Background References](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14445)**  `arXiv:2610.14445`  
  _Jiayi Wu, Tianfu Wang, Rui Zhao, Florian Schiffers, Zhimin Chen, Cornelia Fermuller, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  In film production, chroma keying composites an approved foreground performance into a new environment, but conventional workflows require coordinated background plates and dedicated harmonization. Recent generative methods often require pre-aligned backgrounds, focus on background-conditioned foreground relighting, or represent the environment only through an edited first frame. These restrictions limit background selection, scene composition, and camera motion while adding preparation or editing effort. We present FreeCHROMA, which adapts a pretrained video diffusion model in a parameter-efficient manner for generative video compositing from one to three unaligned background references. The model integrates the foreground into the referenced environment, preserving foreground identity, motion, and fine visual details while generating a spatiotemporally coherent background. Foreground-background harmonization occurs within the same generation process, without a separate relighting stage. Optional text instructions help disambiguate complex spatial relationships and camera behavior. To train the model, we construct pseudo-paired data from readily available real monocular videos through foreground-background separation and augmentation with existing foundation models. The original videos serve as training targets, while automated processing and quality verification enable scalable data construction. Across reference fidelity, foreground preservation, scene integration, harmonization, and overall video quality, FreeCHROMA consistently outperforms recent compositing and conditional video-generation baselines, with particularly clear gains under camera motion.   </details>

- **[VisualCoding: Learning Executable Skills for Reliable Visual Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14403)**  `arXiv:2610.14403`  
  _Liu Jiaqi, Jin Ruinan, Li Xiaoxiao_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>

Execution-Guided Program Acquisition composes visual primitives and additional code into family-level solvers, then iteratively tests and revises them on labeled training instances. - **[RealityBench: Simulated Environments to Evaluate a Vision Language Model's Ability to Document Human Physical Work](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14397)**  `arXiv:2610.14397`  
  _Andrew Perrault, Anmol Takiar, Dominik Wienecki, Arnab Nandi_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Augmenting worker capabilities in the physical world through guidance has been a decades-long goal for AI agents. One key supporting capability is to understand what the worker is doing, seeing through the human's camera or smart glasses, and assist them in documentation. Despite advances in vision language models, their capabilities in these settings remain uncertain and are challenging to benchmark because most physical work data is proprietary, and involves too much variability to study in a principled manner. Unlike structured settings such as kitchens and warehouses that have predictable lighting, geometry, and objects, field-facing tasks such as rooftop solar installation and vehicle repair are unconstrained and high variance. Here, we model real-world physical work in Blender across eleven environments, incorporating variants in both image acceptability and documentation. The acceptability task asks whether a particular view would be suitable proof-of-work and documentation asks whether an agent can understand the task-relevant state of the environment from that view. Across 26 vision-language models, we find that top models largely solve documentation when the answer is text in frame, but are weak at reading measurements and at judging small parts and spatial relations, such as whether a tape measure leans. Acceptability is harder to pin down because human raters disagree with each other. Measured against a scorer that agrees with the raters' majority about as often as a single rater does, the best models cannot be distinguished from a single non-author rater, at a cost within the range of a human pass. In the three environments where we can trace acceptability errors, most wrong rejections come from misreading the scene rather than the requirement. On the three documentation questions for which we have real images, model rankings on rendered frames transfer to real images.
  </details>

- **[Learning Transferable World-Action Models from Task-Paired Human Videos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14351)**  `arXiv:2610.14351`  
  _Jeongeun Park, Taekyung Kim, Dongyoon Han, Sangdoo Yun_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>

However, standard within-video next-frame prediction allows them to rely on appearance shared between the context and future, rather than learning interactions that transfer across scenes and embodiments. We introduce WATCH, a cross-video pre-training that learns from task-paired human demonstrations collected across diverse environments. Conditioned on the video and actions of one demonstration, the model jointly predicts another demonstration's actions and future frames from its current observation. Predicting one demonstration from another encourages the model to learn task-relevant interactions that transfer across scenes and demonstrators. Our pre-training shows that these capabilities can be learned from readily scalable human-human pairs alone, without requiring matched human-robot demonstrations. Analyses before robot post-training show improved motion alignment across embodiments and better action and video prediction on unseen robots, with representations closer to those learned from robot pairs. After robot post-training, WATCH improves MimicDroid in-context success from 40.9% to 68.3% with Cosmos Policy and from 59.8% to 77.7% with Cosmos3, with the largest gains on the unseen levels. - **[TraceSampler: Making Sampling Errors Predictable and Correctable for Accelerated Generative Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14332)**  `arXiv:2610.14332`  
  _George Matthew, Guoqiang Zhang, Kenta Niwa_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Accurate sampling from continuous-time generative models can require many model evaluations. Low-step sampling reduces cost, but coarse updates introduce endpoint errors that can accumulate and degrade generation quality. We introduce TraceSampler, a post-training method that corrects these errors without modifying the pretrained model. Rather than optimising low-step updates directly, TraceSampler models endpoint error as a sample-specific prediction problem. A higher-step reference integration over the same interval provides the supervised target, while a compact representation makes high-dimensional error predictable from the sampling trace. This representation combines shared residual structure, trace-derived directions, and a low-rank remainder, so shallow per-step MLP heads predict sample-dependent coefficients. These coefficients drive a two-stage learned residual correction: the first stage predicts the full endpoint residual, while an intermediate backbone evaluation provides new trace information to predict the remaining residual; this evaluation is reused by the following step. TraceSampler is evaluated with Rectified Flow on CIFAR-10, SiT-XL/2 on ImageNet-256, and SD3.5 Medium for text-to-image generation. At 10 steps, it reduces trajectory MSE relative to matched-step Euler by 90.5% on CIFAR-10 and 85.6% on ImageNet-256, while achieving FID scores of 2.692 and 2.189, close to 120-step Heun references of 2.601 and 2.056 with 24$\times$ fewer backbone evaluations. On SD3.5 Medium, TraceSampler improves image quality and prompt following; at 10 steps, ImageReward rises from 0.752 to 0.906 while trajectory MSE falls by 70.7%. These gains preserve Euler's backbone-evaluation budget, add less than 0.4% inference FLOPs, and incur negligible wall-clock overhead, showing that coarse-step sampling error can be made predictable from the sampling trace and efficiently corrected.
  </details>

- **[Real-Time Traffic Density Estimation: A Hybrid Computer Vision and Predictive Machine Learning Pipeline](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14326)**  `arXiv:2610.14326`  
  _Prince Kwabena Appiah Boadu_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Traffic density estimation from camera feeds requires connecting visual perception with short-horizon forecasting. We present a two-stage pipeline that combines vehicle detection and tracking with a spatial logic layer, followed by a temporal estimator. The spatial layer filters bounding boxes by their overlap with a precomputed road mask and extracts per-frame traffic features. LSTM, GRU, and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) estimators use these features to predict five future steps from a ten-frame input window. We benchmark ten detector variants from six families on a dataset of 5,716 annotated frames using a single NVIDIA GPU. YOLOv5l achieves the highest mAP@50:95 of 0.524 at 56 frames per second, while YOLOv8n reaches 258 frames per second at 0.487 mAP@50:95; these rates measure detector inference without tracking or spatial filtering. Temporal evaluation on 29,243 held-out windows yields aggregate R-squared values of 0.858 for GRU, 0.856 for LSTM, and 0.840 for TCN. These metrics measure forecasts of detector-derived telemetry and are dominated by direction variance, rather than establishing absolute traffic-density accuracy. No road mask was available for the evaluation stream, limiting validation of the spatial filtering component. A live run on a third camera stream examines forecasting behavior within the complete pipeline. The results characterize detector speed-accuracy trade-offs and the limitations of short-window traffic telemetry forecasting.
  </details>

- **[Manifold Navigation Learning Using Recurrent Networks: Efficient Training Techniques](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14325)**  `arXiv:2610.14325`  
  _Sarah Harkins Dayton, Sathya Rengaswami, Vasileios Maroulas, David L. Boothe, Ioannis D. Schizas_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Position tracking is a well-studied problem in Euclidean navigation, yet comparatively little attention has been given to navigation on general manifolds, where motion is governed by the underlying geometry of the space. In this work, we formalize the problem of manifold navigation as a velocity-driven tracking task and propose a coordinate-chart-based learning framework in which learning models operate entirely in a Euclidean representation. Predicted trajectories are mapped to the manifold via an immersion function prior to error computation, allowing geometric consistency to be evaluated without explicitly enforcing manifold constraints during learning. Within this framework, we focus on Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) for sequential position prediction on curved manifolds after comparisons with alternative recurrent architectures. We evaluate our GRU models, trained with pertinent custom loss functions, against both a standard MSE loss function and a naive vector-addition baseline. We evaluate our approach on both analytically (and numerically) defined manifolds, as well as a surface reconstructed from a LiDAR point cloud. Our results show that recurrent models can learn to approximate manifold-constrained dynamics from velocity sequences and consistently outperform Euclidean baselines. Our results demonstrate that certain custom loss functions significantly improve long-horizon prediction accuracy compared to conventional point-wise loss functions.
  </details>

- **[EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14324)**  `arXiv:2610.14324`  
  _Anxhelo Diko, Jieyu Lin, Stefano Ambrogio, Ziyun Li, Mahmoud Assran, Théo Moutakanni, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Foundation models like V-JEPA are increasingly deployed across a heterogeneous edge-cloud continuum spanning smart glasses, phones, robots, and servers. Yet, they are typically trained as rigid, fixed-capacity networks bound to one device, supporting neither reconfigurable compute budgets nor collaborative execution. Existing approaches address only one axis at a time: slimmable and NAS-based methods provide width elasticity but assume single-device inference, whereas split-computing methods enable cross-device collaboration only for fixed partitions and static capacities. We introduce Elastic V-JEPA (EV-JEPA), a single model trained once and deployable everywhere along the continuum. Its width is reconfigurable, and it is natively partitionable across heterogeneous devices. At its core is Transition-Aware Triplet Training (T3). At each step we pick a narrow and a wide width, and train three paths: each width alone, plus a hybrid path that runs the early layers narrow and the rest wide. The hybrid switch point is where one device hands off to another, so the same weights learn both single-device and cross-device execution. Across various benchmarks, EV-JEPA falls within 1 accuracy point of independently trained baselines while improving over previous elastic training approaches by up to 11 accuracy points. Narrow-to-wide cross-device hybrid execution recovers to within 1.1 points of the highest-capacity standalone model and supports many-to-one, any-to-any, and variable-split configurations. Finally, we show that the elastic principle extends beyond the backbone to an elastic token compression mechanism that exposes controllable trade-offs among on-device computation, latency, and accuracy.
  </details>

- **[MvFFN: Multi-view Floor plan Feed-forward Network for Unposed Wide-Baseline Panorama Layout Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14315)**  `arXiv:2610.14315`

  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
